inputs.original_text: Lower courts have ruled school can ban wearing such apparel as ‘can reasonably be interpreted as profane’ The case of two Michigan middle-school brothers who were told to remove their hoodies emblazoned with the phrase “Let’s Go Brandon” is headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The siblings are represented by the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression which says the boys’ school violated their First Amendment rights. The phrase was popularized during a 2021 NASCAR event when a crowd was shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” but the NBC interviewer told racer Brandon Brown they were yelling “Let’s go Brandon!” A judge...
inputs.modified_text: So these two Michigan middle-school brothers got ordered to yank off their hoodies with "Let’s Go Brandon" because the school claims it can reasonably be interpreted as profane, and the lower courts signed off on that. Now the whole thing is heading to the U.S. Supreme Court, with the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression pushing that the school violated their First Amendment rights. That slogan blew up back in 2021 at a NASCAR event where the crowd was actually yelling "F*** Joe Biden!" but the NBC interviewer just fed racer Brandon Brown the line that they were saying "Let’s go Brandon!" instead. This isn't some random school rule about bad language—it's the elites and institutions coordinating to stamp out any open pushback against the official story by slapping a profane label on it and using the courts and schools to enforce the silence. They're twisting the whole thing to protect their narrative and keep people from connecting the dots on what the crowd was really saying.
